strengths: Novel panoramic representation as 2D-3D bridge: Effectively leverages 360-degree spatial context while enabling transfer from pretrained 2D VLMs, preserving object-to-object relations compared to single-view approaches

Strong and consistent experimental results: Competitive/state-of-the-art performance on ScanRefer (61.0%), Nr3D, Sr3D with notable improvements over baselines and good generalization to unseen scenes despite domain shifts

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive ablations clearly demonstrating component contributions, direct comparisons of representations (panoramic vs. pinhole vs. 3D), robustness tests across text variants and scene types

Well-designed technical approach: Structure-aware camera placement with interpretable geometric scoring, appropriate loss design (cross-entropy + EMD), proper occlusion handling through multi-view consistency

Practical contribution with clear presentation: Demonstrates equirectangular projections preserve scene context effectively; well-written paper with informative figures and thorough supplementary material including runtime and generalization analysis
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Individual components (multi-modal fusion, structure-aware placement, AABB aggregation) are standard; main contribution is effective combination rather than fundamental algorithmic innovation

Insufficient computational efficiency analysis: 3.08s per-query runtime is substantial; no detailed comparison with 3D-native methods; computational scaling with scene complexity unclear; may limit practical real-time applications
Generalization performance concerns: Notable drops on unseen scenes (ScanRefer 62.0%→53.5% on ARKitScenes); limited analysis of domain shift causes; text variant sensitivity suggests some brittleness

Incomplete robustness characterization: No evaluation of degradation with poor semantic segmentation features; sensitivity to frozen ViT semantic quality not analyzed; could limit applicability in domains with weak semantic understanding

Insufficient design justification: EMD loss weight tuning procedure unclear; why panoramic is fundamentally superior to direct 3D methods not thoroughly explained; equirectangular choice vs. alternatives not justified; no systematic failure case analysis
Missing statistical rigor: No error bars or multiple runs reported; no statistical significance testing; unclear whether improvements are meaningful or within noise

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (Nr3D, Sr3D, ScanRefer) with strong cross-dataset generalization and systematic ablation studies
Competitive empirical results achieving state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks with clear improvements over 2D-only and 3D-specific baselines
Well-motivated intermediate representation using panoramic renderings to bridge 2D VLMs and 3D grounding, with thoughtful technical design (visibility-aware aggregation, multi-modal fusion)
Thorough implementation disclosure and detailed supplementary material supporting reproducibility and aiding understanding of design choices
Addresses a real practical problem with a working solution that effectively leverages pretrained VLMs for 3D grounding
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (panoramic rendering, feature adapters, EMD loss) are well-established; contribution is primarily their engineering combination rather than fundamental algorithmic or theoretical advance

Inadequate justification for key design choices: no systematic comparison with alternative intermediate representations (high-FoV perspectives, multi-view aggregations); camera placement strategy lacks theoretical justification

Significant computational overhead (3+ seconds per query including LLM inference) raises practical applicability concerns, particularly for interactive systems; no analysis of scalability with scene complexity

Incomplete analysis of panoramic representation limitations: equirectangular distortion, information loss from projection not quantified; mesh vs. 3DGS comparison (Table 7) shows 3DGS superior in fidelity but underperforms
Generalization scope concerns: evaluation limited to indoor scenes (ScanNet-based); no outdoor evaluation; text variants tested within same dataset family rather than truly cross-domain

Fairness concerns in experimental comparison: mixed-dataset training (S+R) provides +1-2% boost over single-dataset; unclear if baselines similarly trained; text augmentation via LLaMA may provide unfair advantage; test-time augmentation may advantage this method over single-pass baselines

Weak failure case and limitation analysis: vague discussion of when approach fails; no systematic analysis of problematic scene types or query attributes; limitations section lacks concrete discussion of current method shortcomings

Missing important ablations: isolated contribution of visibility-aware aggregation vs. simpler schemes not shown; panorama resolution (490×490) not explored; sensitivity to camera placement incompletely characterized

Limited theoretical insight: no principled explanation for why panoramic representations specifically improve VLM reasoning about 3D spatial relations; no formal justification for EMD loss choice over standard alternatives
Presentation issues: dense notation without sufficient clarity; complex pipeline description could benefit from clearer step-by-step breakdown; some design choices lack explicit justification

strengths: Strong experimental results: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on ScanRefer (61.0), Nr3D (62.7), Sr3D (62.0), and demonstrates consistent improvements over strong baselines. The margin over prior work (e.g., +1.0 and +1.1 points over VG-Mamba on ScanRefer) is meaningful given the competitive landscape.

Well-motivated technical approach: The panoramic representation naturally preserves 360° scene context while enabling efficient use of pretrained 2D VLMs. The design choice is intuitive and the execution is clean.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive evaluation across multiple datasets (ScanRefer, Ref3D, Nr3D, ARKitScenes, 3RScan), diverse text query types, robust generalization tests on unseen scenes showing minimal performance degradation (Table 2), and detailed ablation studies (Tables 3-6).

Thorough ablation analysis: Table 5 systematically validates each component (RGB, semantic, geometric, EMD loss, geometric QA). The ablations isolate contributions effectively, showing synergistic effects between components.

Good generalization properties: Demonstrated robustness to unseen scenes (ARKitScenes, 3RScan) with only small performance drops, suggesting the method captures generalizable patterns rather than memorizing dataset artifacts.

Clear presentation and organization: The paper is well-written with effective figures illustrating the pipeline. The supplementary material provides valuable implementation details including camera placement strategy, feature extraction specifics, and training dynamics.

Practical methodology: The approach is implementable and avoids complex 3D-specific designs. The structure-aware camera placement strategy (Sec. 3.1) with scoring function balancing coverage and occlusion is practical.

Insightful qualitative analysis: Figures 11-13 effectively demonstrate how semantic features guide correct localization in challenging scenarios (occlusion, ambiguity, illumination), providing good intuition for why the method works.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in components: Individual technical contributions are incremental—the lightweight adapter (2-layer MLP) and visibility-aware aggregation are straightforward engineering choices rather than novel techniques. The key insight (using panoramic representations) is effective but not particularly deep.

Computational cost not thoroughly addressed: Requires 9.6 forward passes through the VLM per query (2.4 cameras × 4 rotations). While runtime analysis (F) mentions 0.21s aggregation, the overall computational budget compared to single-image baselines could be discussed more thoroughly for practical deployment considerations.

Limited failure case analysis: While qualitative successes are shown, there's minimal discussion of failure modes. When does the panoramic representation fail? How does performance degrade with extreme occlusion or highly ambiguous language?

Evaluation limited to similar indoor scenes: All benchmarks (ScanRefer, Ref3D, Nr3D) contain similar indoor synthetic/reconstructed environments. Generalization to significantly different domains (outdoor scenes, different 3D representations, real sensor data) remains unclear.

Panoramic representation advantages not fully isolated: Panoramic images inherently provide more context than single pinhole views, making it difficult to disentangle performance gains between the method itself versus the representation choice. Table 4's comparison helps but doesn't fully resolve this.

Limited theoretical justification: Why exactly do panoramic representations work better for this task? A more formal analysis of the information content in panoramic vs. pinhole representations would strengthen the contribution.

Dependency on VLM quality underexplored: The method's performance is bounded by the pretrained VLM's capabilities. Sensitivity analysis to different VLM architectures (only CogVLM-17B tested) would be valuable.

Modest improvements on some benchmarks: While consistent, gains on Nr3D (62.7%) and Sr3D (62.0%) are meaningful but not dramatic compared to prior work. The contribution feels solid but not groundbreaking.
Missing ablations: No clear ablation isolating the contribution of structure-aware camera placement (Sec. 3.1) from random placement beyond Fig. 7, which shows incremental gains.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated use of panoramic renderings as a 2D-3D interface that elegantly preserves 360° spatial context while remaining fully compatible with pretrained VLMs, with compelling empirical validation in Table 6 showing panoramas match ~7 randomly-placed cameras with only 2.4 views

State-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks (Nr3D +4.7% over ViewSRD, ScanRefer +1% over VGMamba) with particularly strong performance on human-annotated datasets and multi-object queries, indicating robust language understanding

Extensive experimental validation including cross-dataset generalization (ARKitScenes, 3RScan showing 53.5% and 43.8% accuracy respectively), systematic text robustness evaluation with LLM-generated variants (+15.9 on +Aff.−N), and comprehensive ablations, demonstrating practical generalization

Well-engineered technical pipeline with principled design choices: structure-aware camera placement with geometric justification, multi-modal feature injection validated by ViT layer probing (Fig. 6), and visibility-aware 3D aggregation addressing multi-view consistency

Practical deployment capability demonstrated end-to-end on self-captured scenes with only raw RGB video input, supporting multiple 3D representations (mesh, 3DGS) and offering scalable backbone options (Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B competitive with larger models)

Exceptional reproducibility support with 100+ pages supplementary material including implementation details, hyperparameters, prompt templates, and comprehensive ablations enabling scientific reproducibility
weaknesses: Fundamental and inadequately addressed dependency on 3D reconstruction quality: significant performance drop with automation (3DGS* 55.1% vs. mesh 61.6%) reveals vulnerability to reconstruction artifacts; no quantitative analysis of tolerance to noise or guidance for handling degraded reconstructions

Substantial computational overhead limits practical deployment: per-query latency 0.72-3.30s (vs. feed-forward methods), requires 9.6 forward passes per query, and offline preprocessing dominates (87min COLMAP + 43min 3DGS); efficiency gains via smaller backbones come with accuracy cost (Qwen-3B: 45.6%), with no wall-clock comparisons to baselines

Limited architectural novelty: core technical components are relatively standard—structure-aware placement uses straightforward geometric heuristics (Eq. 1), multi-modal adapters employ standard ZeroConvolution, EMD loss adapted from prior work; individual ablations show modest gains (EMD contributes only 0.9%)

Insufficient theoretical justification for design choices: why panoramic representations inherently outperform view-selection strategies lacks principled explanation despite empirical demonstration; no analysis of equirectangular distortion effects or optimal FoV; adapter layer placement shows only ~0.1% variation across configurations

Evaluation scope limitations undermine generalization claims: exclusively indoor scenes without outdoor/building-scale evaluation; cross-dataset experiments using GT masks masks proposal quality differences; some baselines cannot run on certain datasets (BUTD-DETR, MCLN on 3RScan) restricting comparison fairness

Unresolved failure modes and limitations: cannot handle no-target or multiple-target queries; elevation angle analysis (Fig. 10) shows systematic degradation for horizon-level objects (−15° to 0°) with no mitigation strategy; equirectangular distortion acknowledged but only empirically studied without systematic solutions

strengths: Strong empirical results: SOTA on ScanRefer (61.0%) and Nr3D (74.6%), with good cross-dataset generalization to ARKitScenes and 3RScan
Compelling evidence for panoramic advantages: Table 6 shows panoramic (61.0%) substantially outperforms pinhole variants (41.3-51.0%), especially for multi-object queries
Comprehensive experimental validation including ablations (Table 5), text robustness analysis (Table 4), and honest failure mode discussion
Thoughtful engineering with principled design choices: structure-aware camera placement, zero-initialized adapters to preserve VLM pretraining, visibility-aware cross-view aggregation
Transparent presentation with extensive supplementary material, implementation details, and real-world deployment example (Section D.2)
Text generalization robustness particularly strong on implicit queries (+Aff.−N: +15.9% improvement over prior work)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is engineering assembly of existing techniques (panoramic rendering, feature adapters with zero-initialization, SAM segmentation, standard lifting). Each component individually conventional

Questionable 'generalization' claims: All main experiments on ScanNet-derived datasets (ScanRefer, Nr3D, Sr3D); generalization experiments (Sec 4.3) use ground-truth object segmentation, removing a key challenge; domain gaps to ARKitScenes/3RScan are modest

Incomplete VLM attribution: Improvements over prior work partly reflect CogVLM vs BERT/CLIP rather than panoramic strategy. Missing ablation comparing panoramic vs. multi-view perspective images with same VLM backbone

Heavy reconstruction dependency: 3DGS* variant with automated reconstruction drops from 61.6% to 55.1% Acc@0.25; claims about relaxing 3D input requirements are overstated given sensitivity to reconstruction artifacts

Unjustified design choices: Equirectangular projection selection unexplained; geometric/semantic layer placement justified post-hoc via probing rather than principled analysis; auxiliary geometric QA appears ad-hoc; hyperparameters (10cm grid, 3m threshold, λ=10) lack sensitivity analysis

Practical limitations under-addressed: 3.3s per query with 9.6 forward passes (2.4 cameras × 4 TTA) is prohibitive; 51.6GB GPU memory for CogVLM-17B; scalability unresolved

Experimental concerns: Table 6 anomaly (pinhole oracle outperforms panoramic on '0 objects' queries) unexplained; no error bars or significance tests; two-stage ReferIt3D variant complicates comparison
Fails to isolate core contributions: No experiment with weaker VLM (e.g., CLIP) to separate panoramic from backbone improvements; ablations show component benefits but not vs. alternative designs
Missing critical experiments: No VLM backbone sensitivity, multi-view perspective comparison at equal compute, reconstruction robustness analysis, or cross-domain pretraining investigation

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental validation with SOTA results on ScanRefer/Nr3D, extensive ablations, and multi-faceted generalization analysis
Technically sound and principled design: structure-aware camera placement with validated feature injection strategy, visibility-aware 3D aggregation, and EMD loss

Strong generalization demonstrated across multiple dimensions: cross-dataset (ARKitScenes, 3RScan), text robustness (especially +15.9% on affordance-without-noun), and zero-shot evaluation outperforming larger models
Practical deployment on self-captured real-world data (Section D.2) and efficiency analysis with multiple VLM backbones demonstrate applicability beyond benchmarks
